```diff
+/** @emoji 🧦️ The socket the proxy opened to the upstream. */
+type ProxiedUpstreamSocket = {
+  destroyed: boolean;
+  destroy(): void;
+  unpipe?(destination?: unknown): void;
+};
+
+/** @emoji 🔌️ The part of a dev proxy that sees a websocket upgrade start and the upstream it opened. */
+export type ProxiedUpgradeProxy = {
+  on(event: "proxyReqWs", listener: (proxyReq: { destroy(): void }, request: unknown, socket: ProxiedBrowserSocket) => void): void;
+  on(event: "open", listener: (proxySocket: ProxiedUpstreamSocket) => void): void;
+  on(event: "error", listener: (error: unknown, request: unknown, connection: unknown) => void): void;
+};
+
+/** 🕊️ Destroys the upstream of a proxied websocket when the browser socket ends or closes. The pipe keeps the browser
+ * socket's writable open, so a destroyed page emits `end` and not `close` while the upstream still writes, and a presence
+ * room would keep that learner until idle. Upgrades are paired in the order they were asked for. One that fails before
+ * it opens is taken off the queue, and its request is destroyed if the browser is already gone.
+ * @see https://github.com/http-party/node-http-proxy — `proxySocket.pipe(socket).pipe(proxySocket)` */
+export function closeProxiedSocketWithBrowser(proxy: ProxiedUpgradeProxy): void {
+  const pending: ProxiedBrowserSocket[] = [];
+  const upgraded = new WeakSet<ProxiedBrowserSocket>();
+  proxy.on("proxyReqWs", (proxyReq, _request, socket) => {
+    pending.push(socket);
+    const abandon = (): void => {
+      if (!upgraded.has(socket)) proxyReq.destroy();
+    };
+    socket.on("end", abandon);
+    socket.on("close", abandon);
+  });
+  proxy.on("open", (proxySocket) => {
+    const socket = pending.shift();
+    if (socket === undefined) return;
+    upgraded.add(socket);
+    const drop = (): void => {
+      socket.unpipe?.(proxySocket);
+      proxySocket.unpipe?.(socket);
+      if (!proxySocket.destroyed) proxySocket.destroy();
+    };
+    if (socket.destroyed) drop();
+    else {
+      socket.on("end", drop);
+      socket.on("close", drop);
+    }
+  });
+  proxy.on("error", (_error, _request, connection) => {
+    const index = pending.indexOf(connection as ProxiedBrowserSocket);
+    if (index >= 0) pending.splice(index, 1);
+  });
+}
 //#endregion 🔖️ServeUpgrade
 
```

```diff
-/** @emoji 📝️ Splits an introduction step body into visual paragraphs on blank lines so each

-    .map((paragraph) => paragraph.trim())
-    .filter((paragraph) => paragraph.length > 0);

-/** @emoji 🧲️ Clamps an introduction info box to the viewport. Authored placement uses a visual inset;

-    top: Math.min(Math.max(position.top, inset), Math.max(inset, viewport.height - boxSize.height - inset)),

-/** @emoji 🧭️ Registers the demonstration-targeting resolver for the surface shown by window element

- * polyline) return the first point (or the origin) for every `t`, never throw. */
-export function polylinePointAt(points: readonly { readonly x: number; readonly y: number }[], t: number): { readonly x: number; readonly y: number } {
-  if (points.length === 0) return { x: 0, y: 0 };
-  if (points.length === 1) return points[0];
-  const segmentLengths: number[] = [];
-  let totalLength = 0;
-  for (let i = 1; i < points.length; i++) {
-    const length = Math.hypot(points[i].x - points[i - 1].x, points[i].y - points[i - 1].y);
-    segmentLengths.push(length);
-    totalLength += length;
-  }
-  if (totalLength === 0) return points[0];
-  const targetDistance = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, t)) * totalLength;
-  let accumulated = 0;
-  for (let i = 0; i < segmentLengths.length; i++) {
-    const segmentLength = segmentLengths[i];
-    if (accumulated + segmentLength >= targetDistance || i === segmentLengths.length - 1) {
-      const segmentT = segmentLength === 0 ? 0 : (targetDistance - accumulated) / segmentLength;
-      return {
-        x: points[i].x + (points[i + 1].x - points[i].x) * segmentT,
-        y: points[i].y + (points[i + 1].y - points[i].y) * segmentT,
-      };
-    }
-    accumulated += segmentLength;
-  }
-  return points[points.length - 1];
-}

-/** @emoji 🪡️ Samples a canvas-layer path (`move`/`line`/`quad`/`cubic` segments, in whatever local
- * coordinate space the caller's points are already expressed in — apply layer transforms before calling)
- * into a flat polyline via de Casteljau evaluation — the one parametric-curve evaluator this codebase has,
- * needed because `IntroductionPoint.Curve` resolves through arc-length interpolation over a polyline, not
- * a true parametric curve. `arc`/`close` segments are not sampled (curve targeting degrades to the
- * straight gap between their neighbors); rare enough for a demonstration target to not warrant full SVG
- * arc-to-bezier conversion. */
-export function sampleBezierSegments(
-  segments: readonly {
-    readonly kind?: string;
-    readonly to?: readonly [number, number];
-    readonly ctrl?: readonly [number, number];
-    readonly ctrl1?: readonly [number, number];
-    readonly ctrl2?: readonly [number, number];
-  }[],
-  samplesPerCurve = 16,
-): readonly { readonly x: number; readonly y: number }[] {
-  const points: { x: number; y: number }[] = [];
-  let current = { x: 0, y: 0 };
-  for (const segment of segments) {
-    if ((segment.kind === "move" || segment.kind === "line") && segment.to) {
-      current = { x: segment.to[0], y: segment.to[1] };
-      points.push(current);
-    } else if (segment.kind === "quad" && segment.ctrl && segment.to) {
-      const ctrl = { x: segment.ctrl[0], y: segment.ctrl[1] };
-      const to = { x: segment.to[0], y: segment.to[1] };
-      for (let i = 1; i <= samplesPerCurve; i++) {
-        const t = i / samplesPerCurve;
-        const oneMinusT = 1 - t;
-        points.push({
-          x: oneMinusT * oneMinusT * current.x + 2 * oneMinusT * t * ctrl.x + t * t * to.x,
-          y: oneMinusT * oneMinusT * current.y + 2 * oneMinusT * t * ctrl.y + t * t * to.y,
-        });
-      }
-      current = to;
-    } else if (segment.kind === "cubic" && segment.ctrl1 && segment.ctrl2 && segment.to) {
-      const ctrl1 = { x: segment.ctrl1[0], y: segment.ctrl1[1] };
-      const ctrl2 = { x: segment.ctrl2[0], y: segment.ctrl2[1] };
-      const to = { x: segment.to[0], y: segment.to[1] };
-      for (let i = 1; i <= samplesPerCurve; i++) {
-        const t = i / samplesPerCurve;
-        const oneMinusT = 1 - t;
-        points.push({
-          x: oneMinusT ** 3 * current.x + 3 * oneMinusT * oneMinusT * t * ctrl1.x + 3 * oneMinusT * t * t * ctrl2.x + t ** 3 * to.x,
-          y: oneMinusT ** 3 * current.y + 3 * oneMinusT * oneMinusT * t * ctrl1.y + 3 * oneMinusT * t * t * ctrl2.y + t ** 3 * to.y,
-        });
-      }
-      current = to;
-    }
-  }
-  return points;
-}

-/** @emoji 📌️ Resolves an `IntroductionPoint` to a live viewport pixel. Called every animation frame by a
- * playing demonstration — re-resolving (rather than caching) keeps a drag path glued to a target that's
- * still moving (a resizing panel, an orbiting 3D camera, a panning 2D canvas). `null` means "not
- * resolvable yet" (element not mounted, no surface resolver registered, entity not found/hidden, or a 3D
- * point off-camera) — callers wait and retry next frame rather than treating it as an error. */
-export function resolveIntroductionPoint(point: IntroductionPoint, root: ParentNode | null = document): IntroductionResolvedPoint | null {
-  if (!root) return null;
-  switch (point.kind) {
-    case "element": {
-      const element = root.querySelector(elementIdSelector(point.id));
-      if (!element) return null;
-      const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
-      const [offsetX, offsetY] = point.offset ?? [0.5, 0.5];
-      return { x: rect.left + offsetX * rect.width, y: rect.top + offsetY * rect.height };
-    }
-    case "screen":
-      return { x: point.x, y: point.y };
-    case "screenNormalized":
-      return { x: point.x * window.innerWidth, y: point.y * window.innerHeight };
-    case "window": {
-      const element = root.querySelector(elementIdSelector(point.id));
-      if (!element) return null;
-      const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
-      return { x: rect.left + point.x, y: rect.top + point.y };
-    }
-    case "windowNormalized": {
-      const element = root.querySelector(elementIdSelector(point.id));
-      if (!element) return null;
-      const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
-      return { x: rect.left + point.x * rect.width, y: rect.top + point.y * rect.height };
-    }
-    case "scene": {
-      const resolver = introductionSurfaceResolvers.get(point.id);
-      const projected = resolver?.scenePoint?.(point.position);
-      if (!projected || !projected.visible) return null;
-      return { x: projected.x, y: projected.y };
-    }
-    case "canvas": {
-      const resolver = introductionSurfaceResolvers.get(point.id);
-      const projected = resolver?.canvasPoint?.(point.x, point.y);
-      if (!projected || !projected.visible) return null;
-      return { x: projected.x, y: projected.y };
-    }
-    case "entity": {
-      const resolver = introductionSurfaceResolvers.get(point.id);
-      const geometry = resolver?.entity?.(point.domain, point.entity);
-      if (!geometry || !geometry.visible) return null;
-      if (!geometry.rect) return geometry.point;
-      const [offsetX, offsetY] = point.offset ?? [0.5, 0.5];
-      return { x: geometry.rect.x + offsetX * geometry.rect.width, y: geometry.rect.y + offsetY * geometry.rect.height };
-    }
-    case "curve": {
-      const resolver = introductionSurfaceResolvers.get(point.id);
-      const geometry = resolver?.entity?.(point.domain, point.entity);
-      if (!geometry || !geometry.visible || !geometry.polyline || geometry.polyline.length === 0) return null;
-      return polylinePointAt(geometry.polyline, point.t);
-    }
-    case "domain": {
-      const resolver = introductionSurfaceResolvers.get(point.id);
-      const geometry = resolver?.entity?.(point.domain, point.entity);
-      if (!geometry || !geometry.visible || !geometry.rect || !geometry.domain) return null;
-      const { min, max, axis } = geometry.domain;
-      const t = max === min ? 0 : (Math.min(max, Math.max(min, point.value)) - min) / (max - min);
-      const rect = geometry.rect;
-      // 🎚️ x-axis tracks read left→right with increasing value; y-axis tracks read bottom→top (screen y
-      // decreases upward), matching how a vertical slider's "up" reads as "more".
-      return axis === "x" ? { x: rect.x + t * rect.width, y: rect.y + rect.height / 2 } : { x: rect.x + rect.width / 2, y: rect.y + (1 - t) * rect.height };
-    }
-    default:
-      return null;
-  }
-}
-//#endregion 🎬️DemonstrationResolve
-
-//#region 🎬️DemonstrationIdle
-export const INTRODUCTION_DEMO_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 1600;
-
-type IntroductionPointerPosition = { readonly x: number; readonly y: number };
-
-type IntroductionPointerIdleState = {
-  readonly idle: boolean;
-  /** 🎬️ The real pointer's last observed viewport position (`null` until it has moved at least once) —
-   * lets a demonstration open by traveling from where the user's actual cursor is resting, instead of
-   * materializing out of nowhere near its target. Stable ref identity; read `.current`, don't watch it. */
-  readonly lastPositionRef: React.RefObject<IntroductionPointerPosition | null>;
-};
-
-/** @emoji 💤️ Tracks whether the user's real pointer has been still for `thresholdMs` — the gate a
- * demonstration plays behind — and where it last was. Any `pointerdown`/`wheel`/`keydown`, or a
- * `pointermove` with different coordinates or non-zero movement deltas, resets the timer and flips back
- * to not-idle immediately. Same-coordinate, zero-delta moves are ignored because browsers re-fire them
- * when the DOM mutates under a stationary cursor. `onActivity` runs synchronously inside the native
- * event handler so the visual disappears before React commits the idle-state update. Starts not-idle:
- * a demonstration should only appear once the user has first settled, not the instant a step mounts
- * mid-motion. */
-export function useIntroductionPointerIdle(enabled: boolean, thresholdMs: number = INTRODUCTION_DEMO_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS, onActivity?: () => void): IntroductionPointerIdleState {
-  const [idle, setIdle] = reactHostPort.useState(false);
-  const lastPositionRef = reactHostPort.useRef<IntroductionPointerPosition | null>(null);
-  const onActivityRef = reactHostPort.useRef(onActivity);
-  onActivityRef.current = onActivity;
-
-  reactHostPort.useEffect(() => {
-    if (!enabled) {
-      setIdle(false);
-      return;
-    }
-    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
-
-    const settle = () => {
-      timer = setTimeout(() => setIdle(true), thresholdMs);
-    };
-    const unsettle = () => {
-      onActivityRef.current?.();
-      setIdle(false);
-      if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
-      settle();
-    };
-    const onPointerMove = (event: PointerEvent) => {
-      const previous = lastPositionRef.current;
-      const coordinatesChanged = !previous || event.clientX !== previous.x || event.clientY !== previous.y;
-      const movementChanged = event.movementX !== 0 || event.movementY !== 0;
-      if (!coordinatesChanged && !movementChanged) return;
-      lastPositionRef.current = { x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY };
-      unsettle();
-    };
-    const onOtherInput = () => unsettle();
-
-    window.addEventListener("pointermove", onPointerMove, true);
-    window.addEventListener("pointerdown", onOtherInput, true);
-    window.addEventListener("wheel", onOtherInput, true);
-    window.addEventListener("keydown", onOtherInput, true);
-    settle();
-    return () => {
-      if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
-      window.removeEventListener("pointermove", onPointerMove, true);
-      window.removeEventListener("pointerdown", onOtherInput, true);
-      window.removeEventListener("wheel", onOtherInput, true);
-      window.removeEventListener("keydown", onOtherInput, true);
-    };
-  }, [enabled, thresholdMs]);
-
-  return { idle, lastPositionRef };
-}
-//#endregion 🎬️DemonstrationIdle
-
-//#region 🎬️DemonstrationOverlay
-const INTRODUCTION_DEMO_GESTURE_DEFAULT_CURSOR: Record<IntroductionGesture["kind"], IntroductionCursor> = {
-  leftClick: "pointer",
-  rightClick: "pointer",
-  doubleClick: "pointer",
-  drag: "grab",
-  scroll: "default",
-  orbit: "move",
-};
-
-type IntroductionDemoPointerButton = "left" | "middle" | "right" | "wheel";
-
-type IntroductionDemoFeedbackKind = "leftClick" | "rightClick" | "doubleClick" | "scroll" | "dragLeft" | "dragMiddle" | "dragRight" | "orbit";
-
-type IntroductionDemoVisual = {
-  readonly button: IntroductionDemoPointerButton;
-  readonly modifiers: readonly IntroductionKeyModifier[];
-  readonly feedback: IntroductionDemoFeedbackKind;
-  readonly showDoubleChip: boolean;
-};
-
-/** @emoji 🖱️ Resolves the mini-mouse highlight, modifier chips, and press/trail family for a gesture. */
-export function introductionDemoResolveVisual(gesture: IntroductionGesture): IntroductionDemoVisual {
-  switch (gesture.kind) {
-    case "leftClick":
-      return { button: "left", modifiers: [], feedback: "leftClick", showDoubleChip: false };
-    case "rightClick":
-      return { button: "right", modifiers: [], feedback: "rightClick", showDoubleChip: false };
-    case "doubleClick":
-      return { button: "left", modifiers: [], feedback: "doubleClick", showDoubleChip: true };
-    case "scroll":
-      return { button: "wheel", modifiers: [], feedback: "scroll", showDoubleChip: false };
-    case "drag": {
-      const button = gesture.button ?? "left";
-      const feedback = button === "middle" ? "dragMiddle" : button === "right" ? "dragRight" : "dragLeft";
-      return { button, modifiers: gesture.modifiers ?? [], feedback, showDoubleChip: false };
-    }
-    case "orbit":
-      return {
-        button: gesture.button ?? "right",
-        modifiers: gesture.modifiers ?? ["alt"],
-        feedback: "orbit",
-        showDoubleChip: false,
-      };
-  }
-}
-
-function introductionDemoRippleClass(feedback: IntroductionDemoFeedbackKind, double = false): string {
-  const tone = feedback === "rightClick" || feedback === "dragRight" || feedback === "orbit" ? "right" : feedback === "dragMiddle" ? "middle" : "left";
-  const base = `introduction-demo-ripple introduction-demo-ripple--${tone}`;
-  return double ? `${base} introduction-demo-ripple--double` : base;
-}
-
-/** @emoji 🌐️ A point along the quadratic-bezier arc from `from` to `to`, bulged perpendicular to the
- * straight line between them — an `orbit` gesture reads as a curved rotation around a pivot, visually
- * distinct from `drag`'s straight-line pan/reposition. */
-export function introductionDemoArcPoint(from: IntroductionResolvedPoint, to: IntroductionResolvedPoint, t: number): IntroductionResolvedPoint {
-  const dx = to.x - from.x;
-  const dy = to.y - from.y;
-  const distance = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;
-  const bulge = Math.min(64, distance * 0.35);
-  const controlX = (from.x + to.x) / 2 + (-dy / distance) * bulge;
-  const controlY = (from.y + to.y) / 2 + (dx / distance) * bulge;
-  const oneMinusT = 1 - t;
-  return {
-    x: oneMinusT * oneMinusT * from.x + 2 * oneMinusT * t * controlX + t * t * to.x,
-    y: oneMinusT * oneMinusT * from.y + 2 * oneMinusT * t * controlY + t * t * to.y,
-  };
-}
-
-const INTRODUCTION_DEMO_PHASE_MS = {
-  appear: 250,
-  travel: 600,
-  press: 180,
-  dragMove: 900,
-  release: 180,
-  linger: 500,
-  fadeOut: 250,
-  pause: 900,
-} as const;
-
-type IntroductionDemoPhase = keyof typeof INTRODUCTION_DEMO_PHASE_MS;
-
-const INTRODUCTION_DEMO_NEXT_PHASE: Record<IntroductionDemoPhase, IntroductionDemoPhase> = {
-  appear: "travel",
-  travel: "press",
-  press: "dragMove",
-  dragMove: "release",
-  release: "linger",
-  linger: "fadeOut",
-  fadeOut: "pause",
-  pause: "appear",
-};
-
-function introductionDemoEaseInOutCubic(t: number): number {
-  return t < 0.5 ? 4 * t * t * t : 1 - (-2 * t + 2) ** 3 / 2;
-}
-
-function introductionDemoLerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number {

-const INTRODUCTION_DEMO_APPEAR_OFFSET = { x: -32, y: -32 } as const;

-/** @emoji 🎬️ Ghost-cursor gesture demonstration(s) for an introduction step, mounted by `UIIntroduction`

-/** @emoji 🎬️ The default demonstration for a purely informational step (`interactions.length === 0`, the
- * Next/Done button is the only way to continue) — clicking `ui.introduction.next`, the stable id every
- * such button renders under regardless of its Next/Done label. Used by `UIIntroduction` whenever the step
- * doesn't declare its own `demonstration`, so authors never have to spell this out per step. */
-const INTRODUCTION_DEMO_NEXT_BUTTON_DEMONSTRATION: IntroductionDemonstration = { gesture: { kind: "leftClick", at: { kind: "element", id: "ui.introduction.next" } } };
-//#endregion 🎬️DemonstrationOverlay
-
-export type UIIntroductionProps = {
-  readonly introduction: IntroductionDefinition;
-  readonly stepIndex: number;
-  /** ✅️ Indices into the active step's `interactions` that are done — drives the checklist rows. */
-  readonly completedInteractionIndices?: readonly number[];
-  readonly onStepIndexChange: (index: number) => void;
-  readonly onDismiss: (completed: boolean) => void;
-};
-
-
-/** @emoji 📐️ One row of an introduction step's {@link IntroductionLogo}s, all sharing one computed height
- * so the row fills its full width edge-to-edge with no logo dominating over another — the height isn't
- * guessed: it's solved from the row's measured width and each logo's own natural aspect ratio (`width /
- * sum-of-aspect-ratios`, accounting for the `gap-double` between logos), so it's exactly right for
- * whatever logos a step declares, never distorting any of them. */
-function IntroductionLogoRow({ logos }: { readonly logos: readonly IntroductionLogo[] }) {
-  const rowRef = reactHostPort.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
-  const [rowWidth, setRowWidth] = reactHostPort.useState(0);
-  const [gapPx, setGapPx] = reactHostPort.useState(0);
-  const [aspectRatios, setAspectRatios] = reactHostPort.useState<readonly (number | null)[]>(() => logos.map(() => null));
-
-  reactHostPort.useEffect(() => {
-    const el = rowRef.current;
-    if (!el) return;
-    const measure = () => {
-      setRowWidth(el.getBoundingClientRect().width);
-      setGapPx(parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).columnGap) || 0);
-    };
-    measure();
-    const observer = new ResizeObserver(measure);
-    observer.observe(el);
-    return () => observer.disconnect();
-  }, []);
-
-  const onLogoLoad = reactHostPort.useCallback((index: number, event: React.SyntheticEvent<HTMLImageElement>) => {
-    const img = event.currentTarget;
-    if (!img.naturalWidth || !img.naturalHeight) return;
-    setAspectRatios((prev) => (prev[index] != null ? prev : prev.map((ratio, i) => (i === index ? img.naturalWidth / img.naturalHeight : ratio))));
-  }, []);
-
-  const aspectRatioSum = aspectRatios.reduce<number | null>((sum, ratio) => (sum == null || ratio == null ? null : sum + ratio), 0);
-  const height = rowWidth > 0 && aspectRatioSum != null && aspectRatioSum > 0 ? (rowWidth - gapPx * (logos.length - 1)) / aspectRatioSum : undefined;
-
-  return (
-    <div ref={rowRef} className="flex w-full items-center gap-double" style={{ visibility: height == null ? "hidden" : "visible" }}>
-      {logos.map((logo, index) => {
-        const style = height != null ? { height } : { height: 0, width: 0 };
-        return (
-          <span key={index} className="inline-flex items-center">
-            {logo.href ? (
-              <a href={logo.href} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" className="inline-flex items-center transition-opacity hover:opacity-80">
-                <img src={logo.src} alt={logo.alt} onLoad={(event) => onLogoLoad(index, event)} className={cn("w-auto object-contain", logo.darkSrc && "dark:hidden")} style={style} />
-                {logo.darkSrc && <img src={logo.darkSrc} alt={logo.alt} onLoad={(event) => onLogoLoad(index, event)} className="hidden w-auto object-contain dark:block" style={style} />}
-              </a>
-            ) : (
-              <>
-                <img src={logo.src} alt={logo.alt} onLoad={(event) => onLogoLoad(index, event)} className={cn("w-auto object-contain", logo.darkSrc && "dark:hidden")} style={style} />
-                {logo.darkSrc && <img src={logo.darkSrc} alt={logo.alt} onLoad={(event) => onLogoLoad(index, event)} className="hidden w-auto object-contain dark:block" style={style} />}
-              </>
-            )}
-          </span>
-        );
-      })}
-    </div>
-  );
-}

-/** @emoji 🎓️ Full-screen first-run walkthrough: a single fullscreen glass veil covers the screen, the

- * for the current step; the box silhouette starts with the introduced highlight + thickness pulse, then
- * follows the shared surface-active lifecycle — click activates (primary stroke), click outside returns
- * to normal and never re-enters the introduced pulse for this step; each blank-line body paragraph
- * emphasizes only while the pointer is on that paragraph — see `[data-slot="introduction-body-paragraph"]:hover`
- * in `🎨️ui.css`).
```

```diff
+/** 🧰️ Resolves utilities through exact window ownership; kind requests need an addressed or unique live instance. */
+export function windowUtility(view: PluginViewState, windowId?: string): string | undefined {
+  const requested = windowId ?? view.windowId;
+  if (requested === undefined) return view.activeUtilityId || undefined;
+  const roster = view.windowInstances ?? [];
+  let id = requested;
+  if (!roster.some(window => window.id === requested)) {
+    const candidates = roster.filter(window => window.windowKindId === requested);
+    if (candidates.length) {
+      const instance = candidates.find(window => window.id === view.windowId) ?? candidates.find(window => window.id === view.focusedWindowId) ?? (candidates.length === 1 ? candidates[0] : undefined);
+      if (!instance) return undefined;
+      id = instance.id;
+    }
+  }
+  const utilities = view.activeUtilityByWindowId;
+  return (utilities && Object.hasOwn(utilities, id) ? utilities[id] : view.windowId === id ? view.activeUtilityId : undefined) || undefined;
+}
```

```diff
 /** 🧬️ A compiled owned-schema export, typed as a boolean runtime check so `assert` never narrows its validated subject to `unknown`. */
 type SchemaCheck = ((data: unknown) => boolean) & Pick<ValidateFunction, "errors">;
+
+/** 🪪️ Validates portable immutable-row projections with SQLite and optionally the native central applier. */
+class StableIdentityCheckScript extends BundleScript {
+  async run(args: string[]): Promise<void> {
+    if (args.length > 1 || (args.length && args[0] !== "--native")) throw Error("stable-identity-check accepts only --native");
+    const owner = join(this.repoRoot, "🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🪡️list-delta");
+    const fixtures = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(owner, "🧫️fixtures/🪪️stable-identity/🔣️.json"), "utf8")) as { vectors: { id: string; base: { id: string; value: number }[]; patches: { target: string; row: { id: string; value: number } }[]; accepted: boolean; expected: { id: string; value: number }[] }[] };
+    const { Database } = await import("bun:sqlite");
+    for (const vector of fixtures.vectors) {
+      const database = new Database(":memory:");
+      try {
+        database.run("CREATE TABLE rows (position INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, value INTEGER NOT NULL)");
+        database.run("CREATE TRIGGER immutable_identity BEFORE UPDATE OF id ON rows WHEN NEW.id <> OLD.id BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'identity changed'); END");
+        vector.base.forEach((row, position) => database.run("INSERT INTO rows VALUES (?, ?, ?)", [position, row.id, row.value]));
+        let accepted = true;
+        database.run("BEGIN");
+        try {
+          for (const patch of vector.patches) {
+            const result = database.run("UPDATE rows SET id = ?, value = ? WHERE id = ?", [patch.row.id, patch.row.value, patch.target]);
+            if (result.changes !== 1) throw Error("missing target");
+          }
+          database.run("COMMIT");
+        } catch {
+          accepted = false;
+          database.run("ROLLBACK");
+        }
+        assert.equal(accepted, vector.accepted, vector.id);
+        assert.deepEqual(database.query("SELECT id, value FROM rows ORDER BY position").all(), vector.expected, vector.id);
+      } finally {
+        database.close();
+      }
+    }
+    const nested = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(owner, "🧫️fixtures/🪆️nested-inverse/🔣️.json"), "utf8")) as { vectors: { id: string; base: { id: string; value: number; label: string; parts: { id: string; weight: number }[] }[]; patches: { id: string; patch: { parts: { removed: { id: string; index: number }[]; inserted: { index: number; row: { id: string; weight: number } }[] } } }[]; expected: unknown }[] };
+    for (const vector of nested.vectors) {
+      const database = new Database(":memory:");
+      try {
+        database.run("CREATE TABLE parts (parent TEXT NOT NULL, position INTEGER NOT NULL, id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, weight INTEGER NOT NULL)");
+        vector.base.forEach(row => row.parts.forEach((part, position) => database.run("INSERT INTO parts VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", [row.id, position, part.id, part.weight])));
+        const insert = (parent: string, index: number, row: { id: string; weight: number }): void => {
+          database.run("UPDATE parts SET position = position + 1 WHERE parent = ? AND position >= ?", [parent, index]);
+          database.run("INSERT INTO parts VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", [parent, index, row.id, row.weight]);
+        };
+        const remove = (parent: string, index: number, id: string): void => {
+          assert.equal(database.run("DELETE FROM parts WHERE parent = ? AND position = ? AND id = ?", [parent, index, id]).changes, 1);
+          database.run("UPDATE parts SET position = position - 1 WHERE parent = ? AND position > ?", [parent, index]);
+        };
+        const inverse: (() => void)[] = [];
+        for (const mutation of vector.patches) {
+          for (const row of mutation.patch.parts.removed) {
+            const before = database.query("SELECT id, weight FROM parts WHERE parent = ? AND position = ?").get(mutation.id, row.index) as { id: string; weight: number };
+            remove(mutation.id, row.index, row.id);
+            inverse.push(() => insert(mutation.id, row.index, before));
+          }
+          for (const row of mutation.patch.parts.inserted) {
+            insert(mutation.id, row.index, row.row);
+            inverse.push(() => remove(mutation.id, row.index, row.row.id));
+          }
+        }
+        const projection = () => vector.base.map(row => ({ ...row, parts: database.query("SELECT id, weight FROM parts WHERE parent = ? ORDER BY position").all(row.id) }));
+        assert.deepEqual(projection(), vector.expected, vector.id);
+        inverse.reverse().forEach(replay => replay());
+        assert.deepEqual(projection(), vector.base, vector.id + " inverse");
+      } finally {
+        database.close();
+      }
+    }
+    if (args[0] === "--native") {
+      await runRepositoryCargoTests(["semio-framework-os-kernel"], this.repoRoot, this.invocation, ["--lib", "-E", "test(stable_identity_) | test(nested_inverse_)", "--no-fail-fast"]);
+    }
+    console.log(`[DEBUG] stable-identity-check: identity=${fixtures.vectors.length} nested=${nested.vectors.length} SQLite projection and inverse oracles passed`);
+  }
+}
```

```diff
-/// ✂️ Bounds `messages`, one edit's message ledger entry, to [`ARTIFACT_EDIT_MESSAGE_ENTRY_BYTES`] deterministically, so
-/// no replay yields an unstorable entry and every replica stores the same one: messages are kept worst level first (ties
-/// in recorded order) while they fit and stay in recorded order, and the dropped rest is summarized by one
-/// `mutation.cascade` info at the operation of the first dropped message. A worst message too large on its own keeps
-/// its code with its text cut to fit. Answers whether anything was cut.
-pub fn bound_edit_messages(edit_id: &str, messages: &mut Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>) -> bool {
-    let size = |message: &crate::os_spr::MutationMessage| message.target.iter().fold(ARTIFACT_EDIT_MESSAGE_OWNER_BYTES.saturating_add(message.code.0.len()).saturating_add(message.message.len()), |bytes, segment| bytes.saturating_add(ARTIFACT_EDIT_MESSAGE_TARGET_BYTES).saturating_add(segment.len()));
-    if messages.iter().fold(edit_id.len(), |bytes, message| bytes.saturating_add(size(message))) <= ARTIFACT_EDIT_MESSAGE_ENTRY_BYTES {
-        return false;
-    }
-    let summary = |dropped: usize, op_index: Option<u32>| {
-        let mut summary = crate::os_spr::MutationMessage::info("mutation.cascade", format!("{dropped} more messages"));
-        summary.op_index = op_index;
-        summary
-    };
-    let budget = ARTIFACT_EDIT_MESSAGE_ENTRY_BYTES.saturating_sub(edit_id.len()).saturating_sub(size(&summary(messages.len(), None)));
-    let mut ranked: Vec<usize> = (0..messages.len()).collect();
-    ranked.sort_by_key(|index| std::cmp::Reverse(messages[*index].level));
-    let mut kept = vec![false; messages.len()];
-    let mut used = 0usize;
-    for index in ranked.iter().copied() {
-        let bytes = size(&messages[index]);
-        if used.saturating_add(bytes) > budget {
-            break;
-        }
-        used += bytes;
-        kept[index] = true;
-    }
-    if let Some(worst) = ranked.first().copied().filter(|_| !kept.iter().any(|kept| *kept)) {
-        let message = &mut messages[worst];
-        message.target.clear();
-        let mut cut = budget.saturating_sub(ARTIFACT_EDIT_MESSAGE_OWNER_BYTES).saturating_sub(message.code.0.len()).min(message.message.len());
-        while !message.message.is_char_boundary(cut) {
-            cut -= 1;
-        }
-        message.message.truncate(cut);
-        kept[worst] = true;
-    }
-    let first_dropped = kept.iter().position(|kept| !*kept).map(|index| messages[index].op_index);
-    let dropped = kept.iter().filter(|kept| !**kept).count();
-    let mut flags = kept.into_iter();
-    messages.retain(|_| flags.next().unwrap_or(false));
-    if let Some(op_index) = first_dropped {
-        messages.push(summary(dropped, op_index));
-    }
-    true
-}

-/// ⚡️ The incrementally maintained fold of one store: the live snapshot, the tail undo cache, the supersessions, the prefix ring and the fold frontier.
-pub struct StoreLive<P, Mutation>
-where
-    P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue,
-    Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + self::Mutation<P>,
-{
-    /// ⚡️ The live, incrementally-maintained RAW fold of `initial_snapshot` over every
-    /// `forwards` operation in `applied_edit_ids` order — i.e. exactly what a full
-    /// {@link materialize_document_snapshot} replay computes BEFORE its single final
-    /// {@link Mutation::reconcile} call. Kept in lock-step by every mutating command below instead of
-    /// replaying on every read, so `snapshot()`/`Apply`/`AppendTransaction` are O(new work) instead of
-    /// O(total history). Cold-path commands (checkout/switch/set_state, which reassign
-    /// `applied_edit_ids` wholesale rather than appending) fall back to a full raw-fold recompute —
-    /// see `fold_current`. Differential ground truth: `test_support::assert_live_equals_replay`.
-    current: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Arc<P>>,
-    current_detached: bool,
-    /// 🪢️ `(edit_id, snapshot right before that edit's forwards were first applied)` for
-    /// whichever edit is CURRENTLY the tail of `applied_edit_ids` — refreshed by `Apply`/`AppendTransaction`
-    /// (fresh-edit branch)/`Redo`, left untouched by further amends to the same edit (so it always
-    /// points at the state before the edit as a whole, not before its latest increment). Powers an
-    /// O(1) `Undo` of exactly this edit; any other undo (not the cached tail, or `None`) falls back
-    /// to `fold_current` — always correct, just not always O(1).
-    tail_undo_cache: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Option<(String, Arc<P>)>>,
-    /// ✏️ The effective supersessions `current` was projected with ([`crate::os_spr::HistoryFold::supersessions`]) —
-    /// what {@link reproject} compares a fresh fold against to find the first position whose effective input changed.
-    supersessions: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<EffectiveSupersessions>,
-    /// 🧭️ Retained projections after applied prefixes ([`PrefixSnapshot`]), at most [`PREFIX_SNAPSHOT_RING_CAPACITY`]
-    /// at an adaptive stride: "the state before operation X" costs at most one stride of folds. An entry is valid only
-    /// while its forwards-only digest names the live effective prefix; every evicted entry retires through the snapshot
-    /// retirement factory (or only drops its alias while another owner holds the root), never a bare drop.
-    prefix_ring: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Vec<PrefixSnapshot<P>>>,
-    /// ✂️ The first applied position whose id, forwards or effective input changed since the prefix ring was last pruned: every
-    /// ring entry past it is stale ({@link prune_prefix_ring}).
-    prefix_ring_dirty_from: usize,
-    /// 🧭️ The greatest `(hlc)` event key of the log while the live cursor — applied, redo, checkpoint, alternative and
-    /// supersessions — is exactly that log's fold at this replica's head; `None` until the next full fold proves it again. What
-    /// lets a local edit sorting after every event join the fold as its tail without folding the log ({@link folded_tail}).
-    fold_frontier: Option<(u64, u64, u64)>,
-    /// ⚡️ The generation right after an undo or redo took the tail path ({@link tail_step}): while it still is the
-    /// generation, nothing happened since, so the redo top is the edit that path moved and redoing it is a tail step again.
-    tail_step_generation: Option<u64>,
-    /// 🟰️ Snapshot equality that lets a Report replay stop where it meets the previous projection
-    /// ({@link enable_convergence_early_exit}).
-    snapshot_equality: Option<fn(&P, &P) -> bool>,
-    marker: std::marker::PhantomData<fn() -> (P, Mutation)>,
-}

-    /// 🎯️ MEDIUM-3 (`26/08/16/MUTATION-OUTCOMES-MERGE-POLICIES-AND-FIRST-CLASS-CONFLICTS` J1
-    /// robustness pass): `envelope.conflicts` used to be appended on every rejection/degradation and
-    /// truncated only incidentally (`resolve_conflict`'s `Quarantined`+`Accept` arm discarding the
-    /// re-ingest's own transient conflicts). A peer that keeps sending a batch this replica keeps
-    /// quarantining — `ingest_remote`'s dag never advances on quarantine, so the SAME envelope is
-    /// eligible for redelivery forever — grows this list, and the persisted `.spr`, without bound.
-    /// Two named caps, two different failure modes because `Open`/resolved conflicts carry different
-    /// weight: a resolved (`Accepted`/`Discarded`) conflict is a closed historical fact a UI no
-    /// longer needs enumerated, so it is PRUNABLE — `prune_resolved_conflicts` evicts the oldest
-    /// (lowest push-index, i.e. first non-`Open` entry found scanning from the front) resolved
-    /// conflicts once the total exceeds [`Self::RESOLVED_CONFLICT_CAP`]. An `Open` conflict is a
-    /// pending decision a human/authority has not yet acted on — silently dropping one would erase
-    /// unresolved history, so it is never evicted; instead [`Self::ensure_open_conflict_capacity`]
-    /// is checked BEFORE any state mutation in every call site that might mint one, and refuses with
-    /// a loud, typed `VcsError` (atomic — nothing applied) once open conflicts would exceed
-    /// [`Self::OPEN_CONFLICT_CAP`], forcing existing ones to be resolved before backlog can grow
-    /// further. `edit_messages` (the durable per-edit message ledger) was reviewed for the same
-    /// pattern and deliberately gets NO cap: unlike `conflicts`, it only grows once per edit that
-    /// ever reaches `committed_ids` (`record_edit_messages`/`replace_edit_messages` are never called
-    /// for a quarantined id — its entry is explicitly cleared instead), so its size tracks genuine
-    /// applied-history growth, not redelivery-of-rejected-content amplification; capping it would
-    /// mean silently losing a still-applied edit's own diagnostic record, which is strictly worse.
-    const OPEN_CONFLICT_CAP: usize = 256;
-
-    /// 🎯️ MEDIUM-3: refuses to mint `additional_open` more `Open` conflicts once doing so would push
-    /// this envelope past [`Self::OPEN_CONFLICT_CAP`]. Callers check this BEFORE mutating any store
-    /// field for the call, so a refusal is atomic — see the const's own doc for why open conflicts
-    /// are capped-but-never-silently-dropped rather than pruned like resolved ones.
-    fn ensure_open_conflict_capacity(&self, additional_open: usize) -> Result<(), VcsError> {
-        if additional_open == 0 {
-            return Ok(());
-        }
-        let open_now = self.envelope.conflicts.iter().filter(|conflict| conflict.status == crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Open).count();
-        if open_now + additional_open > Self::OPEN_CONFLICT_CAP {
-            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(
-                "open conflict backlog is at capacity ({open_now} of {} open, {additional_open} more pending) — resolve existing open conflicts before this artifact can record another",
-                Self::OPEN_CONFLICT_CAP
-            )));
-        }
-        Ok(())
-    }

-    async fn replay_mutations(&mut self, store_log: &mut StoreLog<P, Mutation>, pre_snapshot: &P, mutations: Vec<Mutation>, transaction: Option<&protocol::TransactionRef>, identity: &mut EntityIdentityAuthority<'_>) -> Result<(ScratchOwner<Vec<Mutation>>, ScratchOwner<Vec<Mutation>>, Vec<MutationMeta>, ScratchOwner<P>, Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>, Vec<(usize, bool)>), VcsError> {

-                }

-    /// ⏰️ A stamped clock is compared against the document's OWN history, not against the
-    /// wall clock this Store happened to be constructed at. `clock` is seeded
-    /// `HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(0, now_ms())` at construction, so a Store that has published
-    /// no edit of its own carries a machine fact, not a document fact, and rejecting a stamp
-    /// against it refused every first publication whose stamp was minted anywhere but this
-    /// process's `now_ms()`. Once this Store has published an edit, `clock` IS the last edit's
-    /// stamp (the commit path assigns `self.clock = next_clock`), and strictly-after is then
-    /// exactly the hybrid-logical invariant the ordering depends on.
-    ///
-    /// 🔏 The stamped identity travels with the stamped clock: a durable committer hashes its
-    /// canonical command over BOTH before the Store is reached, so an authority that minted its
-    /// own content-addressed `edit_id()` published an edit that no verifier could bind back to
-    /// the approval it executed. It is admitted under the same fixed identity capacity every
-    /// other Store identity answers to.

-    fn begin_apply_batch_owned<A>(
-        &self, store_log: &StoreLog<P, Mutation>, store_wire: &StoreWire<P, Mutation>,
-        operation: semio_framework_job::OperationId,
-        expected_generation: u64,
-        expected_revision: [u8; 32],
-        actor: semio_framework_value::SharedUtf8,
-        lane: HistoryLane,
-        group_id: Option<String>,
-        source: ArtifactStoreBatchSourceOf<P, Mutation, A>,
-        outbound: bool,
-        transaction: Option<protocol::TransactionRef>,
-    ) -> Result<ArtifactStoreBatchPublication<P, Mutation>, ArtifactStoreBatchAdmissionRejected<A::Input>>
-    where
-        P: Sync + Send,
-        A: ArtifactStoreBatchItemAuthority<P, Mutation> + 'static,
-        Mutation: 'static,
-        P: 'static,
-    {
-        let reject = |reason: String, source: ArtifactStoreBatchSourceOf<P, Mutation, A>| ArtifactStoreBatchAdmissionRejected { reason, mutations: source.inputs.into() };
-        if source.inputs.is_empty() {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication requires at least one admitted mutation owner".into(), source));
-        }
-        if store_wire.durable_group_root.is_some() {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication cannot interleave with an unresolved durable group decision".into(), source));
-        }
-        if let Some(open) = store_log.envelope.open_transaction.as_ref().filter(|open| transaction.as_ref().is_none_or(|transaction| transaction.id != open.transaction.id)) {
-            return Err(reject(format!("batched publication cannot interleave with the open tool transaction {}", open.transaction.id), source));
-        }
-        if self.generation != expected_generation || self.content_revision != expected_revision {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication base generation or revision is stale".into(), source));
-        }
-        if lane != HistoryLane::Document {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication has no retained side-lane map preparation authority".into(), source));
-        }
-        if store_wire.backbone.is_some() && !outbound {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication has no retained outbound backbone encoder/sender authority".into(), source));
-        }
-        if actor.is_empty() || actor.len() > ARTIFACT_STORE_ONE_ITEM_ID_BYTES {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication actor exceeds its fixed identity capacity".into(), source));
-        }
-        if group_id.as_ref().is_some_and(|id| id.is_empty() || id.len() > ARTIFACT_STORE_ONE_ITEM_ID_BYTES) {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication group exceeds its fixed identity capacity".into(), source));
-        }
-        let Some(cursor) = store_log.envelope.cursor.as_ref() else {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication requires an initialized live cursor authority".into(), source));
-        };
-        if cursor.applied_edit_ids.len() != store_log.applied_edit_ids.len() || cursor.redo_edit_ids.len() != store_log.redo_edit_ids.len() || cursor.checkpoint_id.as_deref() != store_log.current_checkpoint_id.as_deref() {
-            return Err(reject("batched publication live cursor is stale or lacks preinstalled fixed capacity".into(), source));
-        }
-        let next_sequence_number = match store_log.edit_sequence.checked_add(1) {
-            Some(value) => value,
-            None => return Err(reject("batched edit sequence exhausted".into(), source)),
-        };
-        let mut next_clock = store_log.clock;
-        next_clock.tick(now_ms());

-            None => {}
-        }
-        let stamped_edit_id = match source.authority.as_ref().and_then(ArtifactStoreBatchItemAuthority::stamped_mutation_id) {
-            Some(identity) if identity.0.is_empty() || identity.0.len() > ARTIFACT_STORE_ONE_ITEM_ID_BYTES => {
-                return Err(reject("stamped publication identity exceeds its fixed identity capacity".into(), source));
-            }
-            Some(identity) => Some(identity.0.clone()),
-            None => None,
-        };
-        let admitted_items = source.inputs.len();

-            store_log.mint_witness(),
-            operation,
-            semio_framework_job::Generation(expected_generation),
-            expected_revision,
-            store_log.applied_edit_ids.len(),
-            next_sequence_number,
-            next_clock,
-            actor,
-            store_log.envelope.active_alternative_id.clone(),
-            group_id,
-            stamped_edit_id,
-        ));

-            operation,
-            expected_generation,
-            expected_revision,
-            lane,
-            footprint: ArtifactStoreOneItemFootprint { work_items: 0, retained_bytes: 0 },
-            source_census_completed: 0,
-            source_census_finished: false,
-            admitted_items,
-            authority: Some(authority),
-            authority_retirement: None,
-            source: Some(Box::new(source)),
-            preparation: None,
-            item_closing: false,
-            stage: None,
-            group_preparation: None,
-            retained_checkpoint: ArtifactStoreOneItemCheckpoint::default(),
-            receipt: None,
-            attempts: 0,
-            published: false,
-            cancel_requested: false,
-            close_started: false,
-            fault: None,
-            refused_base: None,
-            refused_authority: None,
-            refused_issuers: [None, None],
-            phase: ArtifactStoreOneItemPublicationPhase::Preparing,
-            verb: None,
-            transaction,
-            outbound,
-            announce_from: 0,
-            announce_items: 0,
-            transaction_open: false,

-    }

-    /// 🎴️ Takes what a finished Report replay publishes — its messages and reached projection — and installs its unit flags

-            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!("replayed edit id {} exceeds its fixed byte authority", entry.edit_id)));
-        }

-    }

-    //#endregion 🔖️EventSourcedHistory
-    /// 🖍️ The applied tail edit's recorded content changed outside a mutation (a group or origin stamp): the next
-    /// {@link bump} rebuilds its revision record.
-    fn restamp_applied_tail(&mut self, store_log: &mut StoreLog<P, Mutation>) {
-        self.mirror_dirt.applied = self.mirror_dirt.applied.min(store_log.applied_edit_ids.len().saturating_sub(1));
-    }
-
-    /// ➕️ Pushes `edit_id` onto the applied stack; its mirrors are stale from the new tail on.
-    fn push_applied_edit_id(&mut self, store_log: &mut StoreLog<P, Mutation>, edit_id: String) {

-        store_log.applied_edit_ids.push(edit_id);
-    }
-
-    /// ➕️ Pushes `edit_id` onto the redo stack; its mirrors are stale from the new top on.
-    fn push_redo_edit_id(&mut self, store_log: &mut StoreLog<P, Mutation>, edit_id: String) {

-        store_log.redo_edit_ids.push(edit_id);
-    }
-
-    /// ➖️ Pops the redo top; its mirrors are stale past the new length.
-    fn pop_redo_edit_id(&mut self, store_log: &mut StoreLog<P, Mutation>) -> Option<String> {

-        self.mirror_dirt.redo = self.mirror_dirt.redo.min(store_log.redo_edit_ids.len());
-        Some(edit_id)
-    }
-}

-    /// 📥️ Pumps every queued inbound message from the attached backbone into the timeline.
-    async fn pump(&mut self) -> Result<bool, VcsError> {
-        self.pump_with_reports().await.map(|(changed, _)| changed)
-    }
-
-    /// 🪆️ A member lane names a document this store does not own; only the composing app can
-    /// resolve `(slot, child_id)` to a live member, so the message waits for its owner.
-    ///
-    /// A store never consumes acks (they flow store→actor); drain and ignore any that echo back.
-    async fn pump_with_reports(&mut self) -> Result<(bool, Vec<crate::os_spr::MergeReport>), VcsError> {
-        let Some(mut backbone) = self.wire.backbone.take() else {
-            return Ok((false, Vec::new()));
-        };
-        let received = backbone.receive().await;
-        self.replace_backbone_retained(Some(backbone))?;
-        let messages = received?;
-        if messages.is_empty() {
-            return Ok((false, Vec::new()));
-        }
-        let mut acked_op_ids: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
-        let mut reports = Vec::new();
-        for message in messages {
-            match message {
-                BackboneMessage::Genesis { pack } => self.verify_genesis(&pack)?,
-                BackboneMessage::Mutations { envelopes } => {
-                    let envelopes = crate::os_spr::decode_envelopes(&envelopes).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;
-                    let op_ids: Vec<String> = envelopes.iter().map(|envelope| envelope.mutation_id.0.clone()).collect();
-                    for envelope in envelopes {
-                        reports.push(self.ingest_remote(envelope).await?);
-                    }
-                    acked_op_ids.extend(op_ids);
-                }
-                member @ BackboneMessage::Member { .. } => self.wire.member_inbox.push_back(member),
-                BackboneMessage::Ack { .. } => {}
-                BackboneMessage::Retract { mutation_ids } => {
-                    self.retract_transitions(&mutation_ids).await?;
-                }
-            }
-        }
-        if !acked_op_ids.is_empty() {
-            if let Some(mut backbone) = self.wire.backbone.take() {
-                let result = backbone.send(BackboneMessage::Ack { op_ids: acked_op_ids }).await;
-                self.replace_backbone_retained(Some(backbone))?;
-                result?;
-            }
-        }
-        Ok((true, reports))
-    }
-}

-/// 🏁️ How a finished replay's drafts are authored: overwrite them in every alternative and checkpoint containing the
-/// operations, supersede them within the existing alternative `alternative_id` only (the line the replay was viewed on — the
-/// undo or redo of a finalize), or keep the originals and branch a new alternative `name` at the head that supersedes them.
-#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
-pub enum HistoryFinalization {
-    Overwrite,
-    Scope { alternative_id: String },
-    Alternative { name: String },
-}
-
-/// ✏️ Where an authored supersession applies: every alternative, one existing alternative, or a new alternative branched at
-/// the head.
-enum SupersedeScope {
-    Document,
-    Alternative(String),
-    NewAlternative(String),
-}
-
-/// 🧾️ One applied operation as history editing addresses it. `effective` describes the operation that folds — the
-/// replacement's leaf (semantic kind, display name) when a valid supersession replaces the recorded input, which the
-/// recorded `meta` never restamps.

-    pub mutation_id: MutationId,
-    pub edit_id: &'a str,
-    pub position: usize,
-    pub op_index: u32,
-    pub operation: &'a Mutation,
-    pub meta: Option<&'a MutationMeta>,
-    pub transaction: Option<&'a protocol::TransactionRef>,
-    pub supersession: Option<&'a protocol::EffectiveSupersession>,
-    pub effective: &'static crate::os_spr::MutationLeafDescriptor,
-    /// 🫷️ The cross-artifact unit the operation belongs to, `None` when it is its own unit ([`ArtifactStore::unit_id`]): an
-    /// operation of a unit takes no supersession in one document alone.
-    pub unit: Option<String>,
-}
```

```diff
-fn parse_canonical_json_value<T>(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<T, DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError>
-where
-    T: ValueToValue + ValueFromValue,
-{
-    validate_json_budget(bytes)?;
-    let json = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|error| DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::Codec(error.to_string()))?;
-    let value = semio_framework_pack_json::from_json_str(json, semio_framework_pack_json::JsonMemberPolicy::Reject).map_err(|error| DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::Codec(error.to_string()))?;
-    if semio_framework_pack_json::to_json_string(&value).as_bytes() != bytes {
-        return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::NonCanonical);
-    }
-    Ok(value)
-}
-
-fn validate_json_budget(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError> {
-    if bytes.len() > DURABLE_OWNED_GROUP_RECOVERY_PACK_MAX_BYTES {
-        return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::RecoveryPackTooLarge);
-    }
-    let mut depth = 0usize;
-    let mut items = usize::from(!bytes.is_empty());
-    let mut in_string = false;
-    let mut escaped = false;
-    for byte in bytes.iter().copied() {
-        if in_string {
-            if escaped {
-                escaped = false;
-            } else if byte == b'\\' {
-                escaped = true;
-            } else if byte == b'"' {
-                in_string = false;
-            } else if byte < 0x20 {
-                return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::NonCanonical);
-            }
-            continue;
-        }
-        match byte {
-            b'"' => in_string = true,
-            b'{' | b'[' => {
-                depth = depth.checked_add(1).ok_or(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::InvalidOutcome)?;
-                if depth > DURABLE_OWNED_GROUP_JSON_MAX_DEPTH {
-                    return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::InvalidOutcome);
-                }
-            }
-            b'}' | b']' => {
-                depth = depth.checked_sub(1).ok_or(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::NonCanonical)?;
-            }
-            b',' => {
-                items = items.checked_add(1).ok_or(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::InvalidOutcome)?;
-                if items > DURABLE_OWNED_GROUP_JSON_MAX_ITEMS {
-                    return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::InvalidOutcome);
-                }
-            }
-            _ => {}
-        }
-    }
-    if depth != 0 || in_string || escaped {
-        return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::NonCanonical);
-    }
-    Ok(())
-}
```

```diff
+fn durable_group_test_outcome<P, Mutation>(recovery_schema: &str, ordinal: u64, member: DurableOwnedGroupTestMember<P, Mutation>) -> Result<DurableStorePreparedOutcomeV1, DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError>
+where
+    P: ArtifactPack + semio_framework_value::retirement::RetireOwned + Sync,
+    Mutation: ValueToValue + ValueFromValue + semio_framework_value::retirement::RetireOwned,
+{
+    let mut owners = super::OneItemOwners::from_returned(member.edit, member.post_snapshot, member.mutation_retirement, member.snapshot_retirement);
+    let outcome = (|| {
+        let (edit, _) = owners.refused.as_ref().expect("original fixture candidates");
+        let actor = edit.actor.clone().ok_or(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::InvalidIdentity)?;
+        let meta = edit.mutation_meta.first().ok_or(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::InvalidOutcome)?;
+        *owners.authority = Some(Arc::new(ArtifactStoreOneItemLiveAuthority::mint(semio_framework_job::OperationId(10_000 + ordinal), semio_framework_job::Generation(ordinal), durable_group_test_revision(format!("durable-group-test-base-{ordinal}").as_bytes()), 0, edit.sequence_number, meta.timestamp, actor, edit.line.clone(), meta.group_id.clone(), None)));
+        let (edit, post) = owners.refused.take().expect("original fixture handoff");
+        match owners.authority.as_ref().expect("original fixture authority").prepare_one_item(edit, post) {
+            Ok(prepared) => *owners.prepared = Some(prepared),
+            Err((error, edit, post)) => {
+                *owners.refused = Some((edit, post));
+                return Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::Preparation(error));
+            }
+        }
+        DurableStorePreparedOutcomeV1::from_prepared(recovery_schema, owners.prepared.as_ref().expect("sealed original fixture"))
+    })();
+    owners.begin_returned_close().expect("original returned fixture cursor admission");
+    while !owners.terminal_is_empty() {
+        let copy = owners.close_demands(0).expect("fixture original copy quote").copy_bytes;
+        let demand = owners.close_demands(copy).expect("fixture original close quote");
+        let grant = semio_framework_value::retained_clone::RetainedCloneGrant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_copy_bytes: demand.copy_bytes, maximum_capacity_bytes: demand.capacity_bytes, maximum_release_bytes: demand.release_bytes, maximum_depth: demand.depth };
+        let step = owners.close_step(grant).expect("caller-issued fixture original closure");
+        assert!(step.progress().fits(grant));
+    }
+    outcome
+}
```

```diff
+fn durable_canonical_planning_preserves_source_and_reports_each_physical_turn() {
+    use semio_framework_trace::observe_heap_allocations_on_this_thread as observe;

+    for source in policy["sources"].as_array().unwrap() {

+        let original: DslValue = semio_framework_pack_json::from_json_str(expected, semio_framework_pack_json::JsonMemberPolicy::Reject).unwrap();
+        let source = super::super::ArtifactCanonicalTreeSource::view(&original);
+        let mut output = planning::DurableCanonicalOutputV1::default();
+        let mut accepted = |_| true;
+        let mut native = NativeEncodeControl::new_retained(&mut accepted);
+        for _ in 0..10000 {
+            if output.ready() { break; }
+            let demand = output.next_demand();
+            let funded = RetainedCloneGrant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_copy_bytes: demand.copy_bytes, maximum_capacity_bytes: demand.capacity_bytes, maximum_release_bytes: demand.release_bytes, maximum_depth: demand.depth };
+            for axis in policy["deniedAxes"].as_array().unwrap() {
+                let mut denied = funded;
+                match axis.as_str().unwrap() {
+                    "items" => denied.maximum_items = 0,
+                    "copyBytes" if demand.copy_bytes != 0 => denied.maximum_copy_bytes -= 1,
+                    "capacityBytes" if demand.capacity_bytes != 0 => denied.maximum_capacity_bytes -= 1,
+                    "depth" if demand.depth != 0 => denied.maximum_depth -= 1,
+                    _ => continue,
+                }
+                let (receipt, heap) = observe(|| output.advance(source, policy["maximumBytes"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize, denied, &mut native).unwrap());
+                assert_eq!(receipt, Default::default());
+                assert_eq!((heap.requested_bytes, heap.released_bytes), (0, 0));
+            }
+            let (receipt, heap) = observe(|| output.advance(source, policy["maximumBytes"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize, funded, &mut native).unwrap());
+            assert!(receipt.fits(funded));
+            assert_eq!((heap.requested_bytes, heap.released_bytes), (receipt.retained_capacity_bytes, receipt.released_bytes));
+        }
+        assert!(output.ready());
+        let actual = output.take(copy_grant(4096).retained_grant()).unwrap().0;
+        assert_eq!(actual, expected.as_bytes());
+        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&actual).unwrap(), serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(expected).unwrap());
+        assert!(output.terminal_is_empty());
+        assert_eq!(semio_framework_pack_json::to_json_string(&original), expected);
+        for boundary in policy["cancelPhases"].as_array().unwrap() {
+            let mut cancelled = planning::DurableCanonicalOutputV1::default();
+            let live = std::cell::Cell::new(true);
+            let mut observer = |_| live.get();
+            let mut native = NativeEncodeControl::new_retained(&mut observer);
+            for _ in 0..10000 {
+                if cancelled.phase() == boundary.as_str().unwrap() { break; }
+                let demand = cancelled.next_demand();
+                let funded = RetainedCloneGrant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_copy_bytes: demand.copy_bytes, maximum_capacity_bytes: demand.capacity_bytes, maximum_release_bytes: demand.release_bytes, maximum_depth: demand.depth };
+                cancelled.advance(source, policy["maximumBytes"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize, funded, &mut native).unwrap();
+            }
+            assert_eq!(cancelled.phase(), boundary.as_str().unwrap());

+            let demand = cancelled.next_demand();
+            let funded = RetainedCloneGrant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_copy_bytes: demand.copy_bytes, maximum_capacity_bytes: demand.capacity_bytes, maximum_release_bytes: demand.release_bytes, maximum_depth: demand.depth };

+        }
+    }

+        for _ in 0..1_000_000{let demand=output.next_demand();let grant=RetainedCloneGrant{maximum_items:1,maximum_copy_bytes:demand.copy_bytes,maximum_capacity_bytes:demand.capacity_bytes,maximum_release_bytes:demand.release_bytes,maximum_depth:demand.depth};let(result,heap)=observe(||output.advance(source,policy["maximumBytes"].as_u64().unwrap()as usize,grant,&mut native));match result{Ok(receipt)=>{assert!(receipt.fits(grant));assert_eq!((heap.requested_bytes,heap.released_bytes),(receipt.retained_capacity_bytes,receipt.released_bytes));},Err(reason)=>{assert!(matches!(reason.kind,semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::DepthLimit|semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::OwnershipLimit));assert_eq!((heap.requested_bytes,heap.released_bytes),(0,0));refused=true;break;}}}

+}

+#[cfg(feature = "durable-group-testing")]
+#[test]
+fn durable_test_fixture_closes_every_original_on_success_and_typed_refusal() {
+    let laws = fixture();
+    for case in laws["helperCases"].as_array().unwrap() {
+        let (parent, parent_weak) = fixture_test_member(case, 1);
+        let (drawing, drawing_weak) = fixture_test_member(case, 2);
+        let (value, value_weak) = fixture_test_member(case, 3);
+        let result = durable_owned_group_journal_test_record_from_edits(reference(&laws["anchor"]["parent"]), parent, drawing, value);
+        assert_eq!([parent_weak.strong_count(), drawing_weak.strong_count(), value_weak.strong_count()], [0; 3], "{} closes all original snapshot strong owners", case["name"]);
+        if let Some(expected) = case["expectedRefusal"].as_str() {
+            let Err(DurableOwnedGroupDecisionError::Preparation(error)) = result else { panic!("fixture retains its typed preparation refusal"); };
+            assert_eq!(error.kind.as_str(), expected);
+        } else {
+            let record = result.unwrap();
+            let decision = DurableOwnedThreeMemberDecisionV1::decode_canonical_pack(record.canonical_pack()).unwrap();
+            for member in [&decision.parent, &decision.drawing, &decision.value] {
+                let bound = DurableBoundOneItemOutcomeV1::decode_canonical_pack(&member.recovery_pack).unwrap();
+                let independent: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bound.edit_canonical_json).unwrap();
+                assert_eq!(independent["forwards"], case["forwards"]);
+                assert_eq!(independent["inverse"], case["inverse"]);
+                assert_eq!(independent["mutationMeta"][0]["group_id"], decision.decision_sha256);
+            }
+        }
+        eprintln!("[DEBUG] durable fixture {} retires all three original roots", case["name"]);
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "durable-group-testing")]
+#[test]
+fn durable_test_fixture_denied_frame_restores_exact_candidates_and_issuers() {
+    let laws = fixture();
+    let denied: semio_framework_value::retained_clone::RetainedCloneGrant = serde_json::from_value(laws["helperRetirementAdmission"].clone()).unwrap();
+    let (member, weak) = fixture_test_member(&laws["helperCases"][0], 1);
+    let edit_pointer = member.edit.forwards.as_ptr();
+    let post_pointer = Arc::as_ptr(&member.post_snapshot);
+    let mutation_pointer = Arc::as_ptr(&member.mutation_retirement);
+    let snapshot_pointer = Arc::as_ptr(&member.snapshot_retirement);
+    let (result, heap) = semio_framework_trace::observe_heap_allocations_on_this_thread(|| super::super::prepared_retirement::ArtifactStorePreparedRetirement::admit_returned(member.edit, member.post_snapshot, member.mutation_retirement, member.snapshot_retirement, denied));
+    assert_eq!((heap.requested_bytes, heap.released_bytes), (0, 0));
+    let Err((error, edit, post_snapshot, mutation_retirement, snapshot_retirement)) = result else { panic!("unfunded returned fixture frame admitted"); };
+    assert_eq!(error.kind, semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::OwnershipLimit);
+    assert_eq!(edit.forwards.as_ptr(), edit_pointer);
+    assert_eq!(Arc::as_ptr(&post_snapshot), post_pointer);
+    assert!(std::ptr::addr_eq(Arc::as_ptr(&mutation_retirement), mutation_pointer));
+    assert!(std::ptr::addr_eq(Arc::as_ptr(&snapshot_retirement), snapshot_pointer));
+    assert_eq!(weak.strong_count(), 1);
+    let member = DurableOwnedGroupTestMember { edit, post_snapshot, mutation_retirement, snapshot_retirement };
+    assert!(durable_group_test_outcome(PARENT_RECOVERY_SCHEMA, 1, member).is_ok());
+    assert_eq!(weak.strong_count(), 0);
+    eprintln!("[DEBUG] durable fixture unfunded frame returns all exact candidates/issuers and then closes funded");
+}
```

```diff
+impl RuntimeMailbox<AppRuntime> {
+    /// 📮️ Every completion remains queue-owned across child pending turns and complete original failures.
+    pub(crate) fn apply_pending_step(&self, cx: &mut semio_framework_job::StepContext<'_>) -> Result<bool, semio_framework_job::OriginalTurnFailure> {
+        if cx.should_yield() || cx.retained_grant().maximum_items == 0 || cx.retained_grant().maximum_depth == 0 { return Ok(false); }
+        let Ok(mut runtime) = self.try_lock() else { return Ok(false) };
+        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
+        if self.recover_original_frame_step(&mut *runtime, cx)? { return Ok(true); }
+        if cx.should_yield() { return Ok(false); }
+        let Ok(mut queue) = self.0.completions.try_lock() else { return Ok(false) };
+        let available = runtime.interaction_available();
+        let head = queue.head_requires_interaction();
+        let owner = queue.interaction_owner_outstanding();
+        let admission = runtime.checkout.admit(head, available, owner);
+        let Some(index) = queue.first_applicable(available) else {
+            if admission == runtime_mailbox_core::InteractionCheckoutStep::Abandoned {
+                return Err(semio_framework_value::ValueError::literal(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvariantViolated, "original interaction checkout has no return owner").into());
+            }
+            return Ok(false);
+        };
+        let selected = &queue.ready[index];
+        if selected.key.is_some() && !(selected.key == Some("window-metrics") && matches!(&selected.apply, RuntimeApply::Resize { .. } | RuntimeApply::Applied)) {
+            return Err(semio_framework_value::ValueError::literal(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvariantViolated, "runtime completion key has no declared scalar revision owner").into());
+        }
+        let removing = matches!(&selected.apply, RuntimeApply::Applied);
+        let child_controls_work = matches!(&selected.apply, RuntimeApply::DispatchEvents(_) | RuntimeApply::ResumeDispatch { .. } | RuntimeApply::ResumeFrameDeferred { .. });
+        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
+        let child_controls_work = child_controls_work || matches!(&selected.apply, RuntimeApply::RestoreInteraction(_));
+        if removing || !child_controls_work {
+            cx.consume_retained(semio_framework_value::RetainedCloneProgress { copied_items: 1, ..Default::default() })?;
+            cx.consume_fuel(1);
+        }
+        let (mut completion, checkout) = queue.checkout_at(index).expect("selected original completion");
+        drop(queue);
+        if removing {
+            if completion.key == Some("window-metrics") { self.0.applied_window_metrics_revision.fetch_max(completion.revision, Ordering::AcqRel); }
+            self.0.completions.lock().unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner).finish_checkout(checkout);
+            return Ok(true);
+        }
+        let stale = completion.key == Some("window-metrics") && completion.revision <= self.0.applied_window_metrics_revision.load(Ordering::Acquire);
+        let result = if stale { Ok(true) } else { completion.apply.apply_step(&mut *runtime, &self.downgrade(), cx) };
+        completion.restores_interaction = completion.apply.restores_interaction();
+        if matches!(result, Ok(true)) { completion.apply = RuntimeApply::Applied; }
+        self.0.completions.lock().unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner).return_checkout(index, completion, checkout);
+        result.map(|_| true)
+    }
+
+    pub(crate) fn pump_pending_applies(&self, credits: u32, cx: &mut semio_framework_job::StepContext<'_>) -> Result<u32, semio_framework_job::OriginalTurnFailure> {
+        let mut applied = 0;
+        while applied < credits && self.apply_pending_step(cx)? { applied += 1; }
+        Ok(applied)
+    }
+
+    /// 👁️ Observes checkout custody without moving a completion or issuing another original caller.
+    pub(crate) fn presenter_interaction_status(&self) -> PresenterInteractionStep {
+        let Ok(runtime) = self.try_lock() else { return PresenterInteractionStep::RuntimeLock };
+        if runtime.interaction_available() { return PresenterInteractionStep::Ready; }
+        let Ok(queue) = self.0.completions.try_lock() else { return PresenterInteractionStep::RuntimeLock };
+        let owner = queue.interaction_owner_outstanding();
+        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
+        let owner = owner || !self.0.original_recovery.try_lock().is_ok_and(|owner| owner.is_none()) || runtime.pending_frame_maintenance_refusal.is_some() || self.0.frame_maintenance_executions.state.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0 || self.0.frame_deferred_executions.state.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0;
+        if owner { PresenterInteractionStep::Waiting { site: runtime.checkout.site().unwrap_or("unknown"), request: shell::host_io_request_trace_label() } } else { PresenterInteractionStep::Abandoned }
+    }
+
+    /// 🤝️ Restores the actual interaction in place while its remaining cursor stays in the same bounded queue.
+    pub(crate) fn restore_presenter_interaction_step(&self, cx: &mut semio_framework_job::StepContext<'_>) -> Result<PresenterInteractionStep, semio_framework_job::OriginalTurnFailure> {
+        if cx.should_yield() || cx.retained_grant().maximum_items == 0 || cx.retained_grant().maximum_depth == 0 { return Ok(self.presenter_interaction_status()); }
+        let Ok(mut runtime) = self.try_lock() else { return Ok(PresenterInteractionStep::RuntimeLock) };
+        if runtime.interaction_available() { return Ok(PresenterInteractionStep::Ready); }
+        let Ok(mut queue) = self.0.completions.try_lock() else { return Ok(PresenterInteractionStep::RuntimeLock) };
+        if let Some(index) = queue.first_interaction_restoration() {
+            let completion = &mut queue.ready[index];
+            if let RuntimeApply::ResumeDispatch { cursor: Some(cursor), .. } = &completion.apply { cursor.validate_original(cx)?; }
+            cx.consume_retained(semio_framework_value::RetainedCloneProgress { copied_items: 1, ..Default::default() })?;
+            cx.consume_fuel(1);
+            completion.apply.restore_interaction_only(&mut *runtime);
+            completion.restores_interaction = completion.apply.restores_interaction();
+            return Ok(PresenterInteractionStep::Restored);
+        }
+        drop(queue);
+        #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
+        if self.recover_original_frame_step(&mut *runtime, cx)? && runtime.interaction_available() { return Ok(PresenterInteractionStep::Restored); }
+        drop(runtime);
+        Ok(self.presenter_interaction_status())
+    }
```

```diff
-describe("Shell dialog origin", () => {
-  it("serializes a seek behind the admitted director write and drains before retirement completes", async () => {
-
-    for (const row of tutorialSerialFixture.cases) {
-      const drive = new TutorialDriveV1();
-      let owner = true;
-      let cursor = 0;
-      const writes: string[] = [];

-        resolve = done;
-      });

-        () => owner,
-        async (token) => {

-          await gate;
-          if (owner && drive.accepts(token)) cursor = 100;
-        },
-      );

-      expect(writes).toEqual(["M"]);

-          writes.push("inverse-M");
-          cursor = 0;

-//#region 🩺️RuntimeDiagnostics
-/** 🩺️ The module that GENERATES the shard worker, read as text. `import.meta.url` is not a file URL
- * under this suite's transform and the module itself cannot be imported here (it reaches the repo
- * library's `bun:sqlite` lease store, which a jsdom bundle refuses), so it is located by walking up
- * from the runner's cwd — the same shape the world3d-host law above uses. */
-function readGeneratedShardWorkerOwnerSource(): string {
-  const relative = "🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🔌️plugin/🌐️browser-bundle/🏗️materialization/🟦️.ts";
-  let root = process.cwd();
-  for (let hop = 0; hop < 12 && !existsSync(`${root}/${relative}`); hop += 1) root = `${root}/..`;
-  expect(existsSync(`${root}/${relative}`)).toBe(true);
-  return readFileSync(`${root}/${relative}`, "utf8");
-}

-describe("shell runtime diagnostics switch", () => {
-  afterEach(() => {
-    setRuntimeDiagnostics(undefined);
-  });
-
-  it("is off by default and names the same key the guest switch does", () => {
-    // 🪞️ `RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_ENV` in `🧰️framework/🔨️modules/⏱️trace/🦀️.rs` — one name, two languages.
-    expect(RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_KEY).toBe("SEMIO_RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS");
-    expect(runtimeDiagnosticsEnabled()).toBe(false);
-  });
-
-  // ⚖️ LAW: the key is spelled once per realm that has to resolve it — the shell, the shard-worker
-  // bootstrap, and the generated worker/host-shim source — and all of them must agree, because the
-  // guest's own `RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_ENV` is the only reader and it matches on the exact string
-  // (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, `📓️audit-guest-tick-cost-2026-09-12.md` §4 rank 1).
-  it("spells the same diagnostics key in every realm that resolves it", () => {
-    expect(SHARD_RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_KEY).toBe(RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_KEY);
-    // 🔌️ The generated shard worker's own copy lives in `🔌️plugin/🌐️browser-bundle/🏗️materialization/🟦️.ts`,
-    // which this jsdom suite cannot import (it reaches the repo library's `bun:sqlite` lease store),
-    // so it is read as text — the same shape `⏱️wgpu-ui-turn-budget` uses for `ShellHost`.
-    const pluginPackage = readGeneratedShardWorkerOwnerSource();
-    expect(pluginPackage).toContain(`export const SHARD_RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_KEY = "${RUNTIME_DIAGNOSTICS_KEY}"`);
-    expect(pluginPackage).toContain(`export const SHARD_WORKER_DIAGNOSTICS_PARAM = "${SHARD_WORKER_DIAGNOSTICS_PARAM}"`);
-  });
-
-  // ⚖️ LAW: an unarmed page boots the shard worker at the bare url, and an armed one stamps the
-  // parameter the worker reads back — the ONLY channel the switch has into a Worker realm, which
-  // owns no `localStorage`. The generated worker must read that same parameter and seed
-  // `wasi:cli/environment` from it, which is what makes the guest's `[TRACE]` sites reachable.
-  it("carries the armed switch into the worker realm on the worker url", () => {
-    const stored = new Map<string, string>();
-    const original = globalThis.localStorage;
-    Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "localStorage", {
-      configurable: true,
-      value: { getItem: (key: string) => stored.get(key) ?? null, setItem: (key: string, value: string) => void stored.set(key, value), removeItem: (key: string) => void stored.delete(key) },
-    });
-    try {
-      expect(shardWorkerUrl()).toBe(SHARD_WORKER_URL);
```
